title: District cap is never checked against the ATTACH spawn tile's own district — cross-boundary estates can exceed the claimed hard bound
detail: Eligibility checks only the cluster's SEED district; the eventual ring tile's district is never cap-checked. Estates straddle Voronoi cells (smaller than the estate radius), so capped districts can gain live terminals, breaking the 'never more than pool tiles' bound.
recommended_fix: In the attach acceptance path, also reject ring candidates whose spawn tile's district (map_district_assign of the tile) is at cap — or narrow the documented claim to seed-district budgets.

title: Spec pin 3 (rich district's estate extends MORE) was never delivered — the attach weighted pick is unpinned against regression to uniform
evidence:
spec-v2-dublin-spawn-director.md §3:
+3. **ATTACH cluster-pick weighting:** two estates in districts of different
+   weights — the rich district's estate extends more (fixture with both
+   clusters eligible); a cluster whose district is at cap is ineligible.

delivered assertion (map_test.odin) is only exclusion + a >0 control:
+	testing.expectf(t, b_spawns > 0, "with the suburb weight restored the suburb district must receive spawns (the exclusion is the weight)")

PR body lists only:
+  ok=false + the 1-tile district), the attach cluster-pick band exclusion
+  (+ positive control), and a board replay byte-identity pin. **Every new
detail: No test compares extension rates with both clusters eligible and unequal weights. Mutating the board attach weighted_pick back to a uniform rng_range passes all eight new pins — the zoom-band ATTACH weighting is effectively unpinned.
recommended_fix: Add a statistical attach pin: two eligible clusters with unequal kind weights (e.g. 4:1), assert the rich district's estate gains the majority of attach spawns.

title: map_board_destroy gained the district_tiles cleanup but the diff shows no matching update to map_board_load_fail's W4 free
detail: district_tiles (with nested per-district lists) is allocated before the terrain/streets parsing that can still fail. The diff updates map_board_destroy but contains no hunk for map_board_load_fail's free list — a missed W4 update leaks on error paths.
recommended_fix: If map_board_load_fail frees fields inline, add the nested district_tiles deletion loop there; otherwise have it delegate to map_board_destroy so the two can never diverge.

title: memlog claims dublin re-bless left 'draw counts unchanged' while spec/PR say the SEED draw went 1 → ≤2 draws
evidence:
.memlog.md (new entry):
+(49/49 log.bin = 8 header bytes @18), dublin 2 T2s re-blessed (cause-documented; draw counts unchanged, values weighted)

spec §1.6:
+- **Dublin re-bless (cause-documented):** the board branch's SEED family
+  changes from 1 draw to ≤2 draws (district pick + tile pick) and the
+  ATTACH cluster pick changes from uniform to weighted (same draw count)

pr-body:
+  went 1 → ≤2 draws + the cluster pick became weighted (values differ;
+  counts identical) — the deliberate dublin behavioral shift
detail: The memlog's blanket 'draw counts unchanged' contradicts the spec and PR body, which both state the SEED family's draw count changed (1 → ≤2). One record is wrong.
recommended_fix: Correct the memlog entry to 'cluster-pick draw count unchanged; SEED draw 1 → ≤2 (district + tile picks)'.

title: dublin-grown usage comment's example '240000ms' is rejected by the verb's bare parse_u64 argument parser
evidence:
dublin_shot.odin:
+// Usage: harness dublin-grown [outdir] [ms]   (default bin/dublin-grown +
+// the demo's own duration; the gate lens extends it — e.g. 240000ms)

main.odin:
+			if v, ok := strconv.parse_u64(rest[1]); ok {
+				run_ms = v
+			} else {
+				fmt.eprintfln("dublin-grown: bad ms %q", rest[1])
+				os.exit(2)
detail: parse_u64('240000ms') fails, so the documented example invocation exits with 'bad ms'. The sibling overlay-check verb's documented trap is the opposite convention (parse_ms requires the suffix).
recommended_fix: Change the comment example to a bare number (240000), or parse with the suffix-tolerant parse_ms used by overlay-check.

title: The district partition derivation is copy-pasted into four builders instead of one shared proc — the exact drift the comments warn against
evidence:
Identical block in map_board_load, test_board, dense_board, and director_board:
+	b.district_tiles = make([dynamic][dynamic]u32, len(b.districts), len(b.districts), allocator)
+	for k in 0..<len(b.candidates) {
+		d := map_district_assign(&b, b.candidates[k])
+		append(&b.district_tiles[d], u32(k))
+	}

growth_test.odin hand-rolls a variant:
+	one.district_tiles = make([dynamic][dynamic]u32, 1, 1, context.temp_allocator)
+	append(&one.district_tiles[0], 0)
detail: Five copies of the partition loop across loader and fixtures; map_district_assign is shared but the build loop is not. The mirror-fixture comment itself names the drift risk a helper would eliminate.
recommended_fix: Extract a shared builder (e.g. map_board_build_district_tiles(b, allocator)) and call it from the loader and every test fixture.
